You’re up well enough. Besides, we haven’t that old tyrant Skeel to deal with now in the classics.”

arxiv-2005-04889.title: FRACTAL BASINS OF ATTRACTION IN A BINARY QUASAR MODEL
arxiv-2005-04889.creator: Vinay Kumar, Pankaj Sharma, Rajiv Aggarwal, Bhavneet Kaur
arxiv-2005-04889.description: Abstract The present paper investigates the binary system of quasars in the framework of the Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The parametric evolution of libration points, the geometry of zero-velocity curves are one of the crucial aspects of our study. The multivariate form of NR method is applied to study the basin of attraction connected with libration points.

arxiv-2012-06708.title: Enabling Input on Tiny/Headless Systems Using Morse Code Conference: Poster at the 2nd Annual Center for Cellular and Biomolecular Machines Open House; October 22, 2018; University of California, Merced, USA
arxiv-2012-06708.creator: Anna-Maria Gueorguieva, Gulnar Rakhmetulla, Ahmed Sabbir Arif
arxiv-2012-06708.description: Abstract . This paper presents results of a pilot study that explored the potential of Morse code as a method for text entry on mobile devices. In the study, participants without prior experience with Morse code reached 6.7 wpm with a Morse code keyboard in three short sessions.

arxiv-2108-12640.title: Tuning magnetocaloric effect by optimizing thickness induced 3D strain state
arxiv-2108-12640.creator: Samir Kumar Giri 1!, Wasim Akram 2!, Manisha Bansal 2, Tuhin Maity 2
arxiv-2108-12640.description: Abstract The effect of 3-dimensional strain state on the magnetocaloric properties of epitaxial La 0.8 Ca 0.2 MnO 3 (LCMO) thin films grown on two types of substrates, SrTiO 3 (001) (STO) and LaAlO 3 (001) (LAO) has been studied as a function of film thickness within the range of 25 – 300 nm.

arxiv-2202-13637.title: Time-dependent generator coordinate method study of fission: dissipation effects
arxiv-2202-13637.creator: Jie Zhao (赵杰), Tamara Nikšić, Dario Vretenar
arxiv-2202-13637.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jie Zhao (赵杰), Tamara Nikšić, Dario Vretenar. Starting from a quantum theory of dissipation for nuclear collective motion, the time-dependent generator coordinate method (TDGCM) is extended to allow for dissipation effects in the description of induced fission dynamics. The extension is based on a generalization of the GCM generating functions that includes excited states, and the resulting equation of motion in the collective coordinates and excitation energy.

arxiv-2206-03470.title: Anomalous Hall conductivity and quantum friction
arxiv-2206-03470.creator: Pavel Středa and Karel Výborný
arxiv-2206-03470.description: Abstract Anomalous Hall effect in high conductivity region is studied using a two-dimensional network model. We find that the off-diagonal conductivity comprises two parts: one which reflects the bulk properties as obtained by the Kubo formula and another which is sensitive to boundary conditions imposed on the network.

arxiv-2211-11653.title: Autonomous Satellite Rendezvous and Proximity Operations with Time-Constrained Sub-Optimal Model Predictive Control Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. Public Affairs approval #AFRL-2022-5517. GB and MH were supported by AFOSR under grant FA9550-19-1-0169, ONR under grants N00014
arxiv-2211-11653.creator: Gabriel Behrendt, Alexander Soderlund, Matthew Hale, Sean Phillips
arxiv-2211-11653.description: Abstract This paper presents a time-constrained model predictive control strategy for the 6 degree-of-freedom (6DOF) autonomous rendezvous and docking problem between a controllable “deputy” spacecraft and an uncontrollable “chief” spacecraft. The control strategy accounts for computational time constraints due to limited onboard processing speed.

arxiv-2301-07397.title: X-ray polarimetry reveals the magnetic field topology on sub-parsec scales in Tycho’s supernova remnant Journal: ApJ Facilities: IXPE, Chandra ixpeobssim ( Baldini et al. 2022 ) , CIAO ( Fruscione et al. 2006 ) , XSPEC ( Arnaud 1996 )
arxiv-2301-07397.creator: Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Patrick Slane, Dmitry Prokhorov, Ping Zhou, Jacco Vink, Niccolò Bucciantini, Enrico Costa, Niccolò Di Lalla, Alessandro Di Marco, Paolo Soffitta, Martin C. Weisskopf, Kazunori Asakura, Luca Baldini, Jeremy Heyl, Philip E. Kaaret, Frédéric Marin, Tsunefumi Mizuno, C.-Y. Ng, Melis
arxiv-2301-07397.description: Abstract Supernova remnants are commonly considered to produce most of the Galactic cosmic-rays via diffusive shock acceleration. However, many questions about the physical conditions at shock fronts, such as the magnetic-field morphology close to the particle acceleration sites, remain open.

arxiv-2302-08144.title: Learning-based solutions to nonlinear hyperbolic PDEs: Empirical insights on generalization errors
arxiv-2302-08144.creator: Bilal Thonnam Thodi, Sai Venkata Ramana Ambadipudi, Saif Eddin Jabari
arxiv-2302-08144.description: Abstract We study learning weak solutions to nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations (H-PDE), which have been difficult to learn due to discontinuities in their solutions. We use a physics-informed variant of the Fourier Neural Operator ( π \pi -FNO) to learn the weak solutions.

arxiv-2306-16899.creator: Maël Dumas, Anthony Perez
arxiv-2306-16899.description: Abstract In the Trivially Perfect Editing problem one is given an undirected graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) and an integer k k and seeks to add or delete at most k k edges in G G to obtain a trivially perfect graph. In a recent work, Dumas et al.

arxiv-2405-11829.title: Adversarially Diversified Rehearsal Memory (ADRM): Mitigating Memory Overfitting Challenge in Continual Learning
arxiv-2405-11829.creator: Hikmat Khan, Ghulam Rasool, Nidhal Carla Bouaynaya
arxiv-2405-11829.description: Abstract Continual learning (CL) focuses on learning non-stationary data distribution without forgetting previous knowledge. Rehearsal-based approaches are commonly used to combat catastrophic forgetting. However, these approaches suffer from a problem called “rehearsal memory overfitting”, where the model becomes too specialized on limited memory samples and loses its ability to generalize effectively.

arxiv-2505-17138.title: RAP : R untime A daptive P runing for LLM Inference
arxiv-2505-17138.creator: Huanrong Liu, Chunlin Tian, Xuyang Wei, Qingbiao Li, Li Li
arxiv-2505-17138.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) excel at language understanding and generation, but their enormous computational and memory requirements hinder deployment. Compression offers a potential solution to mitigate these constraints. However, most existing methods rely on fixed heuristics and thus fail to adapt to runtime memory variations or heterogeneous KV cache demands arising from diverse user requests.

arxiv-2602-11222.title: Elliptic Clausen Functions and Degenerations Circular, Elliptic, and Hyperbolic Parallelism
arxiv-2602-11222.creator: Ken Nagai
arxiv-2602-11222.description: Abstract We introduce a unified elliptic extension of CL-type Clausen functions based on logarithmic primitives of the Jacobi theta function. The resulting elliptic Clausen family satisfies the same integral recursion as the classical circular case, with all differences encoded in boundary constants determined by the underlying logarithmic kernel.

pmc-11709595.title: APOEε4 Allele Modulates Region‐Specific Transcriptomic Changes in Epigenetic Control Pathways: Implications for Late‐Onset Alzheimer’s Disease Risk
pmc-11709595.creator: Nicole Delatorre, Hannah Van Rossum, Anna Parker, Roberta Diaz Brinton
pmc-11709595.description: BackgroundAge, sex, and APOE genotype are well‐established risk factors for late‐onset Alzheimer’s Disease (LOAD). Previous findings demonstrate that neuroinflammatory profiles of the human midlife female brain closely resemble the human AD brain. Given APOE’s role in LOAD pathogenesis, here we investigate the contribution of this risk factor on targeted AD relevant transcriptional pathways.

pmc-12785080.title: Reintroduced Grey Crowned Cranes (Balearica regulorum) Exhibit Reduced Dispersal and Smaller Home Ranges than Wild Conspecifics in Rwanda
pmc-12785080.creator: Deo Ruhagazi, Olivier Nsengimana, Placide Masengesho, Bernard Ndayisaba, Jean Ferus Niyomwungeri, Laura E. Peirson, Richard Muvunyi, Kirsten Szala-Krotkov, Curtice R. Griffin
pmc-12785080.description: Simple SummaryGrey Crowned Cranes are beautiful, endangered birds found across eastern and southern Africa. In Rwanda, many cranes had been captured illegally as chicks and juveniles and kept in captivity as pets for years. To save them, conservationists rescued the birds, rehabilitated them, and released them back into the wild.

pmc-13081488.title: Epidemiological characteristics and LSTM-based simulation of mumps incidence in Ningbo, China from 2005 to 2024
pmc-13081488.creator: Zi Ye, Xiaoxia Zhu, Heng Fan, Weitao Yao, Yanghui Wu, Tianfeng He
pmc-13081488.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to analyze the epidemiological characteristics of mumps in Ningbo, China, from 2005 to 2024, and to develop a predictive model using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to forecast incidence trends.MethodsSurveillance data of mumps cases were obtained from the China National Infectious Disease Network Direct Reporting System (CNIDNDRS).

pmc-13199594.title: Topical editorials, papers and commentaries: next 10 years
pmc-13199594.creator: Aileen A O’Brien, Kamaldeep Bhui, Richard Williams, Jill Stavert, Cornelius Katona, Kenneth R Kaufman
pmc-13199594.description: SummaryEditorials and commentaries have a central role in shaping debate, priorities and values within psychiatry. Reflecting on the first decade of BJPsych Open, we consider how topical writing both responds to and helps define emerging scientific, social, ethical and political challenges.

pmc-13233542.title: Case Report: A case of primary renal synovial sarcoma
pmc-13233542.creator: Xuan Li, Jiahao Su, Zijie Tang, Yuan Li, Xiaogang Feng, Feng Lin, Hanyu Chen, Qizhong Fu, Xujie Liu, Ying Liu
pmc-13233542.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This case report describes a 53-year-old male patient with primary renal synovial sarcoma. He initially presented with intermittent pain in the lumbar and abdominal regions. Imaging revealed a left renal mass measuring approximately 13.3 cm × 11.6 cm. After radical left nephrectomy, pathological diagnosis was confirmed through immunohistochemical analysis and genetic testing, which identified an SS18-SSX2 fusion, leading to a definitive diagnosis of primary renal synovial sarcoma. Postoperatively, the patient received chemotherapy with epirubicin combined with ifosfamide.

pmc-13346589.title: O-54 HOW DO WE KNOW A HEALTH PROTECTION SYSTEM PROTECTS THE POPULATION? USING THE HEALTH PROTECTION ASSURANCE FRAMEWORK TO SEEK CLARITY, ACCOUNTABILITY AND SYSTEM WIDE IMPROVEMENT
pmc-13346589.creator: Miss Nadine Hilliard, Mrs Ania Hewis, Mr David Pearce, Mr Mike Sandys, Dr Jessica Banks
pmc-13346589.description: BackgroundHealth Protection systems (HPs) are complex, multi-agency networks requiring effective cross-sectoral collaboration to protect population health. Launched in 2024, the Health Protection Assurance Framework (HPAF) was developed as a robust, flexible tool to convene professionals across organisational boundaries and stimulate structured dialogue regarding local health protection arrangements.
